title: The first turban
hookLine: a ceremony when a young person ties the full turban for the first time
tomorrow: a teammate asks Simran: is Sikhi yours, or your parents'?

cards: Graduations hand you a cap. Some teams hand a new player a jersey at a little ceremony.
Gurveer, fifteen, from Simran's kirtan class, is getting something stranger: a long length of cloth, starched and folded, and a whole Sunday program built around him tying it.
Simran's dad, Harjit, calls it the day Gurveer gets crowned. Here's the odd part. A crown is something somebody else puts on your head, once, and it's made of gold.
This one is cotton. And Gurveer has to put it on himself.

teach.b: The ceremony is dastar bandi: dastar, the turban, and bandi, tying. Families hold it at the gurdwara, before the Guru Granth Sahib, with Ardas and a hukam, and sometimes an elder helps tie the first one.
Some young women and girls tie a dastar too. Here's something to tell a friend tonight. The turban isn't one of the five Ks.

teach.h: NOT A K: IT KEEPS THE KESH.
teach.b: The dastar is what covers and keeps the kesh, and the Sikh code asks Sikh men to wear one. So why a crown?
Some Sikhs point to a line on ang 1084, in a hymn by Guru Arjan, that pairs a whole, uncut form, sabat soorat, with the dastar on the head, as part of a life given to God.
And tradition says that in the Gurus' time, a turban marked people of rank. The Gurus' Sikhs wore it whoever they were. Which solves the puzzle.
A king is crowned once, by someone above him.

teach.h: A CROWN YOU TIE YOURSELF, DAILY.
teach.b: A Sikh ties this crown with their own hands, again every morning, with no one above them but the Guru.
It's dignity you put on yourself, as a promise. Gurveer gets it a little crooked the first time. Harjit says his own was worse.

how: A dastar bandi is held at the gurdwara before the Guru Granth Sahib, with Ardas and karah prashad, when a young person ties the full turban for the first time; family elders sometimes help tie it.

o: a vow to keep the hair uncut for life
the ceremony of tying a first full turban
a coming-of-age feast held for a family's eldest son

games.q: the cloth crown — tap the pairs.
p: the uncut hair, one of the five Ks

s: the turban is one of the five Ks
kesh, the uncut hair, is; the dastar covers and keeps it.
at a dastar bandi, someone else ties the turban for you, once, like a coronation
an elder may help the first time, but a Sikh ties it with their own hands, every morning.
some young women and girls tie a dastar too
the ceremony isn't only for boys.

games.q: your friend's first turban comes out lopsided at his dastar bandi, and he wants to redo the whole program. what does today offer him?
o: it's a crown he ties himself every morning; the first one's allowed to be crooked.
yes, redo it: the ceremony only counts if the first tie is perfect.
let the granthi tie it for him from now on, so it's always right.
games.why: Gurveer's first was a little crooked, and Harjit said his own was worse. the dastar is retied every day by the one who wears it.

practice: Find a scarf, a dish towel, or any long cloth. Fold it lengthwise into a neat, even band, smoothing each fold with your palm, and tie it once, carefully, around your wrist or your knee.
Then let your hands rest and keep the feel of that care for the sit.

wordCard.voice: Dastar bandi. The ceremony where a young Sikh ties the full turban for the first time, before the Guru.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: dastar, the turban; a dastar bandi is its first tying.

carryVoice: Crowned: by your own hands, every single morning, and a little crooked at first. That's today.

sources.ref: Ang 1084 (Maru, Guru Arjan: sabat soorat dastaar siraa), paraphrased
